run_meta.system_prompt: You are being evaluated. Follow the user message exactly. Do not add instructions, context, or behavior beyond what it specifies.
run_meta.comparability: NOT COMPARABLE to an anthropic-sdk run: max_tokens and thinking are not controllable through the claude-code-cli path, and roughly 1.7k tokens of Claude Code harness context (system prompt scaffolding, even with --tools "" --strict-mcp-config) precede the prompt on every request. effort and the resolved model ARE pinned on this path, the same as on anthropic-sdk, so those two fields — and only those two — can be compared across the two backends.

output.summary: Your store has problems that stop sales outright: shoppers who don't use a mouse can't add a card to the cart, and your collection pages tell search engines not to list them at all. Below that sits a layer of friction — dead links on the home page, slow loading on phones, faint button text, and missing shipping, tax and returns detail at the moments buyers decide. Most are small fixes.

F-02.consequence: Search engines are told not to list your collection pages, so shoppers searching for cards never find them.
F-02.affects: Anyone who would have arrived from a search engine.
F-02.change: Remove the tag telling search engines not to list the collection template.

F-01.consequence: A shopper using a keyboard or a screen reader cannot add a card to the cart at all.
F-01.affects: Every visitor who does not use a mouse.
F-01.change: Rebuild the add-to-cart control as a real button element.

F-07.consequence: The collection page moves while it loads, so taps and clicks land on the wrong card.
F-07.affects: Everyone browsing collections, most of all on phones.
F-07.change: Have a developer identify what shifts during load and reserve space for it.

F-04.consequence: Shoppers tap the main home page links and nothing happens, so browsing stops before it starts.
F-04.affects: Every visitor who lands on the home page.
F-04.change: Point the hero and category links at their real destination pages.

F-09.consequence: Search results and browser tabs show the same generic label, so nothing tells a shopper what the page holds.
F-09.affects: Anyone finding you through search, and anyone with tabs open.
F-09.change: Write a distinct title for the home page and for each collection.

F-14.consequence: The home page never states plainly what you sell, leaving shoppers and search engines to work it out.
F-14.affects: Every home page visitor, and search engines reading it.
F-14.change: Add a main heading to the home page describing what the shop sells.

F-03.consequence: Text on the main buttons is hard to read, so shoppers hesitate at the moment they would buy.
F-03.affects: Anyone with low vision, and anyone shopping in bright light.
F-03.change: Darken the button colour or lighten its text until the two contrast clearly.

F-05.consequence: A shopper on a phone waits at a mostly blank product page long enough that many give up.
F-05.affects: Mobile shoppers, who are most of your traffic.
F-05.change: Have a developer find what delays the product page on phones and reduce it.

F-08.consequence: Pages pull down far heavier images than they actually display, so shoppers wait on their data for nothing.
F-08.affects: Every visitor, most noticeably mobile shoppers on cellular data.
F-08.change: Serve images sized to how large they appear on the page.

F-16.consequence: Shoppers reach the cart without knowing what shipping costs, and some leave rather than find out at checkout.
F-16.affects: Every shopper who reaches the cart.
F-16.change: Show shipping cost, and any free-shipping threshold, in the cart.

F-17.consequence: The cart total isn't the final total, so tax and any duty arrive as a surprise at checkout.
F-17.affects: Every cart shopper, especially anyone buying across the border.
F-17.change: State in the cart that tax, and duty where it applies, are added at checkout.

F-18.consequence: Nothing on the product page says whether a card can be returned, so cautious buyers hesitate before committing.
F-18.affects: Anyone deciding whether to buy a card.
F-18.change: Add a returns and refund statement to the product page.

F-19.consequence: Shoppers can't tell when a card would arrive, so anyone buying for a date or occasion stalls.
F-19.affects: Every shopper on a product page.
F-19.change: State expected delivery or shipping times on the product page.

F-10.consequence: Search results show whatever text they can scrape from these pages, which rarely reads like an invitation to click.
F-10.affects: Anyone who sees these pages in search results.
F-10.change: Write a meta description — the search-result summary — for each of these pages.

F-11.consequence: Supporting text on collection and product pages is faint enough that some shoppers simply cannot read it.
F-11.affects: Shoppers with low vision, and anyone on a phone outdoors.
F-11.change: Darken the muted grey text until it reads clearly against its background.

F-12.consequence: Screen reader users can't tell what a field is asking for, and the hint disappears for everyone once typing starts.
F-12.affects: Anyone using a screen reader, and anyone filling a form.
F-12.change: Add a visible label to every form field instead of relying on placeholder text.

F-15.consequence: Screen reader users hear the file names of the trust badges instead of the reassurance those badges carry.
F-15.affects: Shoppers using a screen reader on the home page.
F-15.change: Rewrite the badge alt text to say what each badge means.

F-06.consequence: The home page takes a noticeable beat to show anything on a phone, and impatient visitors leave first.
F-06.affects: Mobile shoppers arriving on the home page.
F-06.change: Have a developer find what delays the home page on phones and reduce it.

F-21.consequence: Some product page copy is written to address automated tools rather than shoppers, and it also sits in the page's hidden metadata.
F-21.affects: Anyone reading that product page, plus tools that read it.
F-21.change: Review that product page copy and its hidden metadata, and remove text not meant for shoppers.
